title: Polynomial Structural Calculus
objective: Implement ordinary exact Python contracts for univariate polynomial composition, reversal, truncation, shifts, integral, resultant, and discriminant across ZZ, QQ, and GF(p), with Sage-compatible edge semantics and representative benchmarks

handoff.summary: Added an ordinary CPython-parseable low-to-high dense polynomial calculus for composition, reversal, truncation, monomial shifts, formal integration, Sylvester resultants, and discriminants. Parent-sensitive division is explicit: callers choose ZZ-to-QQ widening, finite-field integer inversion, and exact Bareiss quotients. Focused Sage.js/CPython tests pin Sage 10.9 behavior for zero and constant polynomials, negative truncation, explicit reverse degree, signed resultants, pivoting, noninvertible characteristic-p antiderivatives, and nonmonic characteristic-p discriminants whose derivative degree drops. A representative dynamic benchmark covers ZZ, QQ, and GF(65521).
risks: The helper deliberately does not choose public polynomial parents. Integration must coerce composition operands, widen ZZ integrals to QQ, and decide whether zero.discriminant() returns the generic parent's zero polynomial object or the specialized exact parent's scalar base-ring zero; the storage helper returns coefficient-domain zero.

The cubic Bareiss implementation is a portable correctness fallback and oracle, not the production path for large resource-backed resultants or discriminants; mature FLINT declarations should remain the accelerated path.
The first native validation attempt failed because this new worktree lacked its ignored local M4RI prefix. After building M4RI, the complete native suite passed without source changes.
next_steps: Add structural_calculus.py to pyrightconfig.json and polynomial-structural-calculus.cjs to test/node-test-manifest.cjs in the integration lane.
Wire public PolynomialElement methods through the lazy polynomial-algorithms boundary, using one coefficient decode for the dynamic fallback and public-parent coercion before calling these helpers.

Add declared FLINT resource-to-resource operations for large ZZ/QQ composition, reverse/shift, resultant, and discriminant where benchmarks justify them; keep these same semantics as the differential oracle.
